mentions.title: WARNING!! Check all KING brand bearings before install
mentions.snippet: An explicit buyer-warning thread on the BMW e90post forum telling other builders to inspect King-brand bearings before installing them. The title alone is a direct caution against the brand, which makes it the most damaging item in today's set.
mentions.replyNote: Still returns HTTP 403 Forbidden; thread content could not be read.

mentions.title: WARNING about King Main Thrust Bearings
mentions.snippet: A buyer-warning thread on a diesel truck forum specifically about King main thrust bearings. Framed as a warning to other builders rather than a question, and the thread remains open and unresolved.
mentions.replyNote: Readable today for the first time after months of 403s: no King or official reply, thread still open and unresolved, last post dated 3 June 2026.

mentions.title: King Main Bearings Defective
mentions.snippet: BMW M5/M6 forum thread reporting King STDX thrust bearings measuring over 1mm too narrow to fit multiple different engine blocks, across both S85 and S65 engines. More than one build affected, which points at a part-spec problem rather than a single bad set.
mentions.replyNote: Still 307-redirects to the tollbit.m5board.com mirror instead of returning thread content; redirect not followed.

mentions.title: King Bearings?
mentions.snippet: Speed-Talk thread in which a builder reports a 2024-production King main bearing that King technical support confirmed was out of specification on free spread, and says he would not use them; he raises concern that 2025 production may share the issue. Other posters in the same thread report no problems.
mentions.replyNote: Thread read successfully; still no King or official brand representative reply and it remains open and unresolved.

mentions.title: King Bearing - lack of professional help for quality control problem
mentions.snippet: A customer received an unopened King package containing a wrong mix of bearing sizes and says King directed him to his supplier rather than resolving it. The complaint is about the service response as much as the part, and the title itself is damaging in search results.
mentions.replyNote: Still returns HTTP 403 Forbidden; thread content could not be read.

mentions.title: Just call it what it is---King Bearings are no longer an option....
mentions.snippet: DSM forum thread arguing King bearings are effectively off the table for 6-bolt engines because of long-running back-order and availability problems since COVID. One poster notes the 7-bolt MB5209XP appears to have returned after more than a year unavailable.
mentions.replyNote: Still returns HTTP 403 Forbidden; thread content could not be read.
